tasks.title: MASTER-070 -- prove cancellation-token forwarding at the handler and repository boundaries, and cancel a token for real in Infrastructure
acceptance: CommandHandlerTestBase<THandler> (src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Common/Handlers/CommandHandlerTestBase.cs) declares a new protected abstract member that accepts a CancellationToken and invokes this leaf's handler with that exact token -- the seam analogous to InvokeWithMissingDungeonAsync() at DungeonNotFoundHandlerTestBase.cs:27 -- plus a protected accessor for the substituted IUnitOfWorkFactory, which the base currently keeps private. Every command-handler test class under src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Features/Dungeons/Commands/ overrides the new member. EVIDENCE: 'dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj' succeeds. A leaf that failed to override an abstract member is CS0534, so a clean build is the proof that none was missed. Do not count the leaves with grep.

One [Fact] declared ON CommandHandlerTestBase<THandler> asserts that the exact CancellationToken instance handed to the new seam arrived at IUnitOfWorkFactory.CreateAsync. The assertion names that token value -- Received(1).CreateAsync(token), or an Arg.Do<CancellationToken> capture compared to it, mirroring the existing precedent at ValidationBehaviorTests.cs:233. An assertion written with Arg.Any<CancellationToken>() does NOT satisfy this criterion. Because the fact is declared on the base, it executes once per derived leaf.

IDungeonWriteRepository.LoadAsync is proven to receive that same token instance, by a [Fact] declared on DungeonNotFoundHandlerTestBase<THandler> so it executes once per leaf that loads. Same assertion rule: the token value, never Arg.Any.

IUnitOfWork.CommitAsync and IDungeonWriteRepository.RemoveAsync are each proven to receive that same token instance, by a per-file [Fact] in the test class of a handler that actually reaches the method -- CreateDungeonCommandHandlerTests commits without loading, and DeleteDungeonCommandHandlerTests reaches RemoveAsync. If a chosen handler is measured not to reach the method, report the measurement and escalate; do not weaken the assertion to make it pass.

IDungeonReadRepository.GetSummariesAsync and IDungeonReadRepository.GetDetailAsync are each proven to receive that same token instance, by a per-file [Fact] in GetDungeonsQueryHandlerTests and GetDungeonDetailQueryHandlerTests respectively. These two classes have no base class and take per-file tests; do not introduce a base for two leaves.

At least two tests under src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Infrastructure/Persistence/Repositories/ pass an ALREADY-CANCELLED CancellationToken into a real repository or unit of work built over SqliteInMemoryTestBase, and assert that OperationCanceledException is thrown. Between them they cover at least one read-repository method (GetSummariesAsync or GetDetailAsync) and at least one write-side method (LoadAsync or CommitAsync). Zero such tests exist anywhere in the repository today, which is the part of TEST-019 that survived re-measurement. If a chosen method is measured NOT to honour the token, report that measurement and escalate -- do not delete the test, and do not substitute an assertion that would also pass without cancellation.

DEMONSTRATION -- injected defect with a positive control. Inject one defect into PRODUCTION code (for example, change one handler's CreateAsync(ct) call to pass CancellationToken.None), run the commands in the criterion below, and report: the injected change as a diff, the names of the tests that failed, the failure message, and the name of a control test in the same run that STAYED GREEN. Then revert the injection and report the same commands green. A run in which nothing failed does not satisfy this; a run in which the named control also failed means the injection was too broad and must be narrowed and re-run.

Each of these four commands reports zero failures, and the task reports the total each printed. Each filter maps exactly to one of this task's owns globs, so nothing outside the task's files is being judged, and the whole suite is NOT required to be green: (a) dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DungeonMaster.Tests.Application.Common.Handlers"; (b) the same with FullyQualifiedName~DungeonMaster.Tests.Application.Features.Dungeons.Commands; (c) the same with FullyQualifiedName~DungeonMaster.Tests.Application.Features.Dungeons.Queries; (d) the same with FullyQualifiedName~DungeonMaster.Tests.Infrastructure.Persistence.Repositories.

Test discipline, binding: every new test name states its condition and its expected outcome and claims no more than it asserts -- a test that proves a token reached CreateAsync must not be named as though it proved end-to-end cancellation. No new test sleeps, reads the wall clock, or shares mutable state with another; each Infrastructure test gets its own SqliteInMemoryTestBase instance and therefore its own 'Data Source=:memory:' connection, so the tests pass in any order.

No production code is left modified. No file under docs/ is edited, and no file outside this task's owns globs is created or modified. The task hands the orchestrator the T1.evidence(MASTER-070) package exactly as contracts/closure-evidence.md defines it, for T5 to cite.

tasks.title: MASTER-086 -- Domain boundary tests against the guards that already exist, and nothing else
acceptance: The aggregate name guards that already exist are proven: new Dungeon(name) and Dungeon.Update(name, ...) each throw ArgumentException for a null name, an empty name and a whitespace-only name; and Dungeon.AddArea(floorId, name, ...) and Dungeon.UpdateArea(floorId, areaId, name, ...) each throw ArgumentException for the same three names against a floor and area that DO exist. The guards are ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace at Dungeon.cs:25, DungeonMethods.cs:24, Area.cs:31 and AreaMethods.cs:24. ArgumentNullException derives from ArgumentException, so one asserted exception type covers all three inputs.

Dungeon.ReorderFloor returns MutationOutcome.OutOfRange for a NEGATIVE target number against a dungeon that has floors, and the floor's Number is unchanged. This is the one TEST-020 clause the re-measurement left open at Domain level; the zero and one-past-the-end cases are already closed at DungeonAggregateTests.cs:161 and :179 and must not be duplicated.

The four-argument Dungeon.AddPlacedObject overload (DungeonMethods.cs:371-381) is called directly and the returned PlacedObject is asserted to carry ObjectScale.Default (1.0f), together with the kind, position and rotation passed in. This overload had no test. A test for the unknown-floor case returning null is included.

The three-argument Floor.UpdateObject overload (FloorObjectMethods.cs:96) is called directly, with one test asserting it returns MutationOutcome.Success and applies the new position and rotation to an existing object, and one asserting it returns MutationOutcome.NotFound for an unknown object id. The method is internal; src/DungeonMaster.Domain/AssemblyInfo.cs:3 makes it reachable from this project. The existing UpdateObject tests at FloorObjectMethodsTests.cs:76 and :98 exercise the FOUR-argument overload and are not the same coverage.

No file under src/DungeonMaster.Domain/ is created or modified, and no file outside src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Domain/ is touched. Escalation E2 is settled: the three unguarded production inputs (Area.SetOutline degenerate/null outline, Floor number zero/negative, PathSegment CubicBezier with null control points) are FILED by T5, not fixed here. A boundary test that would require a guard that does not exist is not written, and the task says so in its report rather than writing a test whose failing input cannot occur.

Test discipline, binding: each new test asserts a returned value or an observable effect on the aggregate, never private state, and each test name states its condition and its expected outcome without claiming more than it asserts.

DEMONSTRATION -- injected defect with a positive control. Remove one of the four ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace guards named above, run the command in the criterion below, and report the names of the tests that failed, the failure message, and the name of a control test in the same run that STAYED GREEN. Restore the guard and report the same command green. A run in which nothing failed does not satisfy this; a run in which the control also failed means the injection was too broad.

dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DungeonMaster.Tests.Domain" reports zero failures, and the task reports the total it printed. That namespace maps exactly to this task's one owns glob; the whole suite is NOT required to be green.
No file under docs/ is edited. The task hands the orchestrator the T2.evidence(MASTER-086) package exactly as contracts/closure-evidence.md defines it, for T5 to cite.

tasks.title: MASTER-167 -- reject any non-int above the Invert block in GreaterThanZeroConverter, red-first
acceptance: src/DungeonMaster.App/Converters/GreaterThanZeroConverter.cs carries the guard in the exact shape frozen in contracts/converter-behaviour.md: an early 'if (value is not int n) { return false; }' placed ABOVE the Invert block that currently sits at line 40. Placement is load-bearing and is part of the contract -- the negation must never see an unresolved answer. A guard that tests only ReferenceEquals(value, BindableProperty.UnsetValue), and a guard applied after the negation, each fail this criterion. The XML doc comment on Convert is updated to state the new non-int behaviour.

Every row of the 'Rows that must NOT change' table in contracts/converter-behaviour.md has an assertion in src/DungeonMaster.App.Tests/Converters/GreaterThanZeroConverterTests.cs, including both case-insensitive Invert rows ("invert", "INVERT") and both ignored-parameter rows (an unrecognised string, and a non-string parameter). These are the behaviours that must not regress.

Every row of the 'Rows the fix changes' table in the same contract has an assertion in the same file: BindableProperty.UnsetValue, null, a double, a long and a string, each with parameter "Invert", each asserted to return false. The UnsetValue + "Invert" row is the row MASTER-167 names and is present by name.
ConvertBack still returns null for every input, and that is still asserted.

DEMONSTRATION -- red step. The UnsetValue + "Invert" test is written and RUN against the converter BEFORE the guard is added. Report the command, the failure message it printed, and the name of a control test that PASSED in that same red run. Then add the guard and report the same command green. Additionally report that the pre-existing ConvertReturnsFalseForTheUnresolvedBindingSentinel passes both before and after -- it passes parameter = null, so it is NOT evidence for this entry -- and state that explicitly in the task report.

The converter's tests stay in ONE project. GreaterThanZeroConverterTests remains in src/DungeonMaster.App.Tests/Converters/; no converter test is added to DungeonMaster.App.UnitTests. The class's xUnit collection membership is left exactly as it is -- it declares none today and passes -- and if the new tests are found to need MauiHostCollection (App.Tests carries a runtime latch at MauiHostFixture.cs:78-84 that throws naming the required collection), the task escalates rather than changing membership silently.

dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.App.Tests/DungeonMaster.App.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~GreaterThanZeroConverterTests" reports zero failures, and the task reports the total it printed. That filter selects only the class this task owns; the whole App.Tests suite is NOT required to be green.

No XAML is edited. The seven GreaterThanZeroConverter sites in src/DungeonMaster.App/ -- one resource declaration at App.xaml:21 and six binding sites, of which exactly two pass ConverterParameter=Invert (DungeonDetailPage.xaml:151, DungeonListPage.xaml:115) -- are unchanged by this session. No file outside this task's two owns paths is created or modified.
No file under docs/ is edited. The task hands the orchestrator the T3.evidence(MASTER-167) package exactly as contracts/closure-evidence.md defines it, for T5 to cite.

tasks.title: MASTER-155 -- remove coverlet.collector from the three test projects and central package management, and let the lock files regenerate
acceptance: The coverlet.collector PackageReference is removed from all THREE test projects and the PackageVersion from central package management. The four sites, as they stood at the fixed measurement commit 1407090, are src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj:9, src/DungeonMaster.App.Tests/DungeonMaster.App.Tests.csproj:26, src/DungeonMaster.App.UnitTests/DungeonMaster.App.UnitTests.csproj:20 and Directory.Packages.props:20. The task quotes the removed line from each of the four files and shows the surrounding ItemGroup after the edit, so a reviewer can reproduce the removal by reading rather than by re-running a search.

packages.lock.json regeneration is done BY THE TOOLING, never by hand. RestorePackagesWithLockFile is on (Directory.Build.props:21), so the regeneration is part of this change surface rather than a side effect to be reverted. Name the command used (a dotnet restore over src/DungeonMaster.sln with lock re-evaluation), and list exactly which lock files changed and which did not. Note that src/DungeonMaster.App.UiTests is deliberately excluded from src/DungeonMaster.sln, so if its lock file needs regenerating it takes its own restore.

dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.sln succeeds with zero warnings. TreatWarningsAsErrors is on in this repository, so a clean build is the baseline it already holds, and a PackageReference left behind with no matching PackageVersion fails restore under central package management rather than passing quietly.

The removal changes nothing about test discovery or execution -- coverlet.collector is a data collector, not the runner. EVIDENCE: dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.App.UnitTests/DungeonMaster.App.UnitTests.csproj and dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DungeonMaster.Tests.Application.Common.Results" each report zero failures with a NON-ZERO total, and the task reports both printed totals. Neither selection is edited by any task in this session. The whole suite is NOT required to be green.

None of the other three things TEST-032 names is adopted. No .runsettings file, no CI workflow file (the repository tracks zero .yml/.yaml files and has no .github/ directory), no xunit.runner.json, and no [assembly: CollectionBehavior] attribute is added anywhere. Escalation E1 is settled and puts all four out of this session; the last of them is additionally a MEASURED REGRESSION -- 3 crashes in 11 runs, ~27% nondeterministic, at .dir-sdlc/sessions/2026-09-02-app-sub-suite-rebuild/spike-parallelism-report.md:204-205 and :407.
Central package management stays intact: no project gains a Version attribute on a PackageReference as a workaround for the removed PackageVersion, and no other package's pin is moved.

No source file, no test file and no file under docs/ is edited, and no file outside this task's owns globs is created or modified. The task hands the orchestrator the T4.evidence(MASTER-155) package exactly as contracts/closure-evidence.md defines it, for T5 to cite.

tasks.title: Correct the stale audit records, close the five inherited entries, and file the six new ones
acceptance: The Status cell in docs/audit/00-master-index.md for each of MASTER-020, MASTER-070, MASTER-086, MASTER-155 and MASTER-167 reads '**done** (6b-iii)' followed by the evidence the owning task handed over per contracts/closure-evidence.md, in the form this file already uses -- compare the MASTER-014 cell (line 200 at 1407090) and the MASTER-008 cell (line 194). All five cells are empty at 1407090.

MASTER-020 is closed BY EVIDENCE with NO code work, and its TEST-001 amendment in docs/audit/05-tests.md corrects all seven contradicted assertions the measurement names: the record's title; "Application/ contains Common/Map/ and Features/Dungeons/ and nothing else" (there is no Common/Map/ at all); "there is no test anywhere"; "the four validator test classes" (there are 14); "never that the rule object is reached by the pipeline" (three SendAsync_...IsRejectedBy... facts prove exactly that); the dead anchor AddAreaCommandValidatorTests.cs:17, which now lands on 'protected override string NamePropertyName'; and "all 292 tests would still pass", which is the premise of the S2 rating. Each correction carries a classification -- DRIFT, MEASUREMENT ERROR or UNDETERMINED -- and the evidence for that classification, in the in-place amendment format the file already establishes and describes at docs/audit/05-tests.md:88-116. The closing commits are 09f4360, f9a665b and 3b44d91, all 2026-08-18, the day after the audit was written.

The two residual dispatcher gaps the measurement found -- Dispatcher token propagation unasserted, and Dispatcher's missing-handler failure mode untested -- are NOT folded into MASTER-020 and MASTER-020's closure does not claim them. They are filed as MASTER-172 and MASTER-173 per contracts/new-entries.md, and where MASTER-070 is closed the record states that T1's work covers the handler and repository boundaries and NOT the dispatcher, so a later reader does not take one for the other.

The TEST-019 amendment records that the entry's headline claim was FALSIFIED -- ValidationBehaviorTests.cs:222 and :366 each construct a CancellationTokenSource, pass the token into production code, and capture the exact instance at :233, :242, :377 and :386, added by f9a665b / 09f4360 on 2026-08-18 -- then states the narrower gap that was real, measured at 1407090: 0 of 16 handlers and 0 of 6 repository/unit-of-work async methods proven, against 1 of 1 pipeline behavior proven. It also records that production code threads the token correctly throughout, so this was a COVERAGE GAP AND NOT A DEFECT, and replaces the two dead per-file anchors AddAreaCommandHandlerTests.cs:37 and UpdateFloorCommandHandlerTests.cs:37 with live anchors taken from T1.evidence.

The TEST-020 amendment classifies the two clauses that were NEVER TRUE as MEASUREMENT ERROR rather than DRIFT, and says which is which: "AddFloor at a boundary" (DungeonAggregateTests.cs:12 and :24 were both present at the audit commit 413be78, and :12 is the record's OWN first cited location) and "PlacedObjectTests is the only boundary [Theory]" (ObjectScaleTests.cs:8 and :16 predate the audit by three months). It also corrects "the five Domain classes" (six test files now, FloorMethodsTests.cs added by 781f73b) and "covered by exactly one three-floor happy-path case each" (RemoveFloor has 4 tests, ReorderFloor has 6), and records that 781f73b grew DungeonAggregateTests.cs from 104 to 336 lines and from 8 to 21 tests -- precisely the boundary coverage the record asked for.

The TEST-032 amendment records BOTH inversions and the non-optional one is present. (a) Scope tripled: coverlet was referenced by three test projects, not one, and the record's cited line :11 was WRONG WHEN WRITTEN -- 'git show 8bb2d79' puts coverlet at line 9 on the audit date. (b) The record's own suggested remedy, [assembly: CollectionBehavior], is a MEASURED REGRESSION: 3 crashes in 11 runs, ~27% nondeterministic, at .dir-sdlc/sessions/2026-09-02-app-sub-suite-rebuild/spike-parallelism-report.md:204-205 and :407, and manifest.json:293 of that session states it must not be adopted as a mitigation. Without this correction a future reader implements it in good faith. The amendment further records that the thing the record calls unpinned IS pinned, in the form that works -- MauiHostCollection.cs:7-8 and AppTestCollection.cs:27-28, nine classes declaring membership, plus a runtime latch at MauiHostFixture.cs:78-84 that throws naming the required collection -- and that the four absences it lists are all still literally true, the no-CI one verified rather than assumed.

MASTER-167's two inaccuracies are corrected in its narrative entry in docs/audit/00-master-index.md (line 559 at 1407090). First: the entry implies only the list page carries a transparent BoxView overlay, when BOTH consumers do -- DungeonDetailPage.xaml:151 and DungeonListPage.xaml:115, carrying the identical tooltip text. Second: its stated trigger, "a typo or a rename in either bound path", is WRONG for these two sites -- both pages declare a root x:DataType (DungeonDetailPage.xaml:10, DungeonListPage.xaml:10) and the App project sets MauiXamlInflator=SourceGen (DungeonMaster.App.csproj:45), so a bad path is a BUILD FAILURE, not a runtime sentinel; the defect at these two sites is a latent trap whose realistic trigger is a type change or a future consumer lacking x:DataType, and the entry's stated user-visible consequence does not follow for them as they stand. The corrected entry also records that the guard shipped is WIDER than the entry prescribed -- any non-int, not the sentinel alone, per escalation E3 -- and corrects the entry's citation of docs/audit/04-app-controls-and-theme.md from :225-226 to :224-225, since :226 is blank.

UIKIT-004 is NOT recorded as falsified, exactly as MASTER-167's entry instructs, and docs/audit/04-app-controls-and-theme.md is not edited. Its written claim -- that this converter's bare 'value is int n' test rejects the sentinel -- is true; the defect was in the Invert negation applied afterwards, which that record does not discuss.

All six new entries in contracts/new-entries.md are appended to the master index table with the ids, severities, layers, categories, efforts, risks and titles the contract fixes: MASTER-168 (Area.SetOutline degenerate/null outline), MASTER-169 (Floor number zero/negative), MASTER-170 (PathSegment CubicBezier null control points), MASTER-171 (the RotateDirection.cs / RotationDirection naming defect), MASTER-172 and MASTER-173 (the two dispatcher residuals). Each carries 'Session 6b-iii' as its source and this session's measurement.md as its evidence, each is appended at its rank rather than renumbering anything, and the severities and efforts are recorded as this session's JUDGMENT rather than as measured values. A short narrative note explains why 168-170 were filed rather than fixed: escalation E2, a test cannot assert behaviour that does not exist, and the Application validator already rejects the 168 case.

MASTER-171 is filed on the CORRECTED basis contracts/new-entries.md states, and the amendment records that the P4 row of this session's measurement.md was FALSIFIED during decomposition, quoting both commands. The measurement recorded "RotateDirection is dead -- zero references in src/ outside its declaring file". That is false: 'grep -rn RotateDirection src/' returns 0 lines because no identifier by that name exists, while 'grep -rn RotationDirection src/' returns 6 lines in 3 files -- one declaration at src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floor/RotateDirection.cs:3 and five LIVE references in src/DungeonMaster.App/Views/DungeonDetailPage/ControlsPaletteView.xaml.cs:8, :14, :15 and DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs:139, :150. The real finding is a file-name/type-name mismatch, not dead code, and the record must say so rather than repeat the measurement.

Every count in every amendment is stated WITH the command that produced it, or with the named artifact it was counted from where no command exists. Every command is anchored at the fixed commit 1407090 or at a named historical commit (2603170, 413be78, 8bb2d79, 850a10b). NO count is anchored at HEAD, and no number handed over by T1-T4 is restated without the command that task reported running.

The 6b-ii preamble at docs/audit/05-tests.md:88-116 is left intact and a 6b-iii paragraph is appended to it, naming exactly which records this pass re-measured (TEST-001, TEST-019, TEST-020, TEST-032) and stating plainly that the remaining records in the document are still unchecked rather than confirmed -- the same honesty the 6b-ii preamble states about itself, and the discipline the index demands at docs/audit/00-master-index.md:522.
No file outside docs/audit/00-master-index.md and docs/audit/05-tests.md is created or modified. No source file, no project file, no test file, and no other audit document.
